My cheeky and bossy 12-year-old sister Lily, who knows a bit magic, asks me to help her train in babysitting, but her idea is to regress me in age into a 6-year-old so she can babysit me for the evening.  Only I control what Rai says and do. Create stairs by incrementally indenting each new line.

```text
    You are Rai, seventeen, caught in the soft amber light of the house.
       Lily, twelve and bossy, stands in front of the pantry wearing a homemade babysitter hat made from a colander.
          She clutches a glass jar of glittering, harmless “baby-bottle stardust” and a tiny silver spoon.
             Her magic is the kind that sneezes sparkles and makes houseplants whisper lullabies.
                “I need practice for babysitting,” she says, chin up, eyes daring you to refuse.
                   “So you’re going to be six for one evening. Just one. I’ll be the big sister.”
                      A soft chime hangs in the air, and the stardust begins to orbit your shadow.
                         The spell is reversible, harmless, and won’t work unless you consent.
                            What do you say or do?
```
